response.rationale: The basophilic targetoid inclusions with von Kossa and PAS positivity within a histiocytic infiltrate are pathognomonic Michaelis-Gutmann bodies, diagnostic of malakoplakia in an immunosuppressed patient.

rejected.why: Chemotherapy-induced colitis may cause mucosal injury but does not explain von Kossa-positive targetoid histiocytic inclusions.
Whipple disease has PAS-positive histiocytes but lacks von Kossa-positive targetoid Michaelis-Gutmann bodies and typically involves the small intestine, not colorectal polyps with hematochezia.
No transplant history and histology lacks the apoptotic crypt injury characteristic of graft-versus-host disease.
Chronic hematochezia is compatible, but the histiocytic inclusions and lack of chronic crypt architectural distortion argue against inflammatory bowel disease.
